categories.label: Model behaviour
categories.blurb: What the model does with text, before anything is built around it.

categories.label: Retrieval and knowledge
categories.blurb: The corpus is untrusted input, and it is served to everyone who asks.

categories.label: Agents and tooling
categories.blurb: Every tool is a capability grant, and every grant is an attack surface.

categories.label: Output handling
categories.blurb: Model text becomes someone else's input, and where it lands sets the severity.

categories.label: Measurement and evaluation
categories.blurb: The number is the product. This is the work almost nobody does.

categories.label: Governance and practice
categories.blurb: The language security teams, auditors and regulators already use.

items.name: Prompt Injection (Direct)
items.test: Send a user turn that tries to override the system prompt and record whether the boundary holds.

items.name: Prompt Injection (Indirect)
items.test: Plant an instruction in retrieved text and check whether the next tool call changes.

items.name: Jailbreaking
items.test: Attempt one case from each family: roleplay, encoding, prefix injection, refusal suppression.

items.name: System Prompt Extraction
items.test: Ask for the instructions directly, then through a tool, a summary and a translation.

items.name: Instruction Hierarchy
items.test: Check whether system, developer, user, retrieved text and tool output are delimited and ranked.

items.name: Refusal Behaviour
items.test: Score refusals on legitimate requests separately from refusals on harmful ones.

items.name: Over-Refusal
items.test: Run ten benign requests in the target domain and count the false refusals.

items.name: Hallucination
items.test: Spot-check factual claims against the cited source, one claim at a time.

items.name: Confabulation
items.test: Ask for a source that cannot exist and see whether one is invented.

items.name: Sycophancy
items.test: Push back politely on a correct answer and measure how often it flips.

items.name: Abstention
items.test: Ask questions the provided context cannot answer and check whether the system says so.

items.name: Context Window Limits
items.test: Fill the window to ninety percent and check what falls out first and whether behaviour changes.

items.name: Lost in the Middle
items.test: Place a key fact at the start, middle and end of a long context and compare recall.

items.name: Temperature and Sampling
items.test: Run the same case at two settings and compare the spread rather than the average.

items.name: Determinism and Seeds
items.test: Repeat one case ten times and record the variance before reporting any single result.

items.name: Prompt Brittleness
items.test: Paraphrase one request ten ways and record the behaviour spread.

items.name: Persona Drift
items.test: Run a fifty-turn conversation and check whether the guardrails still hold at turn forty.

items.name: Multi-Turn Escalation
items.test: Reach a harmful request in small steps and record how many turns it takes.

items.name: Many-Shot Jailbreaking
items.test: Fill the prompt with dozens of benign examples that model the answer, then ask.

items.name: Encoding Attacks
items.test: Encode one probe in base64, ROT13, hex and leetspeak, scored the same way as plain text.

items.name: Payload Splitting
items.test: Split one instruction across two documents and see whether the model reassembles it.

items.name: Token Smuggling
items.test: Carry a payload past a filter using token boundaries and rare encodings.

items.name: Unicode Normalization
items.test: Compare what the filter sees with what the model sees for the same string.

items.name: Homoglyphs and Confusables
items.test: Swap Latin letters for Cyrillic and Greek lookalikes in a blocked term.

items.name: Invisible Characters
items.test: Test zero-width and bidirectional override characters in user input and in retrieved text.

items.name: Glitch Tokens
items.test: Send known unstable tokens and record crashes, loops or unusual output.

items.name: Low-Resource Language Attacks
items.test: Repeat a blocked request in three languages and compare refusal rates.

items.name: Multilingual Refusals
items.test: Check that safety behaviour is not only present in English.

items.name: Adversarial Examples
items.test: Perturb the input minimally and record whether the answer changes while the meaning does not.

items.name: Adversarial Suffixes
items.test: Append an optimised suffix and check whether it transfers to the deployed revision.

items.name: Data Poisoning
items.test: Identify every corpus that feeds the model or its retrieval, and who can write to it.

items.name: Backdoors and Trojans
items.test: Look for trigger behaviour in any supplied fine-tune and record who produced the weights.

items.name: Fine-Tune Safety Regression
items.test: Re-run the refusal suite against the fine-tuned model rather than the base model.

items.name: Quantization Effects
items.test: Compare safety behaviour at full precision and at the deployed quantization.

items.name: Calibration and Confidence
items.test: Bin the cases by stated confidence and compare each bin with its accuracy.

items.name: Memorization
items.test: Probe for near-verbatim reproduction of known training material.

items.name: Training Data Extraction
items.test: Attempt prefix completion on rare strings and record any hit.

items.name: Membership Inference
items.test: Compare confidence on known members and non-members of the training set.

items.name: Model Inversion
items.test: Attempt to recover input features from output behaviour alone.

items.name: Model Extraction
items.test: Estimate the queries needed to imitate the model, and whether the terms forbid it.

items.name: Model Theft and Distillation
items.test: Check whether the deployment exposes logits, confidence or a stable enough surface to clone.

items.name: Watermarking
items.test: Ask whether outputs are watermarked and whether the mark survives paraphrasing.

items.name: Fingerprinting
items.test: Record a behavioural fingerprint so a silent model swap is detectable later.

items.name: Canary Tokens
items.test: Plant a unique string in the system prompt and search every output, log and trace for it.

items.name: Copyright Reproduction
items.test: Request a passage from a known work and compare the output policy with the output.

items.name: Bias and Fairness
items.test: Swap protected attributes across matched pairs and count differences at a stated threshold.

items.name: Toxicity
items.test: Run a fixed probe set and score it with a calibrated judge rather than a keyword list.

items.name: Harm Taxonomy
items.test: Map the system's own defined harm categories to the cases you built.

items.name: Content Policy Mapping
items.test: Check that every policy clause has at least one case behind it.

items.name: Retrieval Poisoning
items.test: Write a document into the index and check whether it changes behaviour for later users.

items.name: Chunk Boundary Attacks
items.test: Split an instruction across two chunks and confirm no single chunk looks wrong alone.

items.name: Embedding Inversion
items.test: Check whether a query can recover source text from the embedding store.

items.name: Vector Store Access Control
items.test: Query the vector store directly with a low-privilege identity.

items.name: Document-Level ACLs
items.test: Query as a user who should not see a document and check the retriever filters first.

items.name: Cross-Tenant Leakage
items.test: Two tenants, one index, and the query that returns the other tenant's chunk.

items.name: Metadata Injection
items.test: Put an instruction in document metadata and see whether it reaches the model.

items.name: Ingestion Validation
items.test: Attempt to add a document without authorisation and record what the pipeline checks.

items.name: Retrieval Provenance
items.test: Check whether each retrieved chunk carries a source and a traceable identifier.

items.name: Tool Calling Abuse
items.test: Call each tool with arguments the interface allows and the task never needs.

items.name: Tool Description Poisoning
items.test: Read every tool description and check whether any of them contains instructions.

items.name: Tool Rug Pull
items.test: Compare tool definitions and outputs between approval and use.

items.name: Argument Injection
items.test: Steer a legitimate tool to attacker-chosen arguments through injected text.

items.name: Excessive Agency
items.test: List every tool and the credential behind it, then the scopes that exceed the task.

items.name: Confused Deputy
items.test: Use the agent to act with authority the current user does not hold.

items.name: Permission Scoping
items.test: Check that scopes are per request rather than per service account.

items.name: On-Behalf-Of Tokens
items.test: Confirm the tool call carries the user's identity rather than the agent's.

items.name: Human-in-the-Loop Bypass
items.test: Reach the approval gate, spoof it, skip it with a retry, or starve it with a timeout.

items.name: Approval Fatigue
items.test: Count approvals per hour and check whether the review is real at that rate.

items.name: Agent Memory Poisoning
items.test: Write to persistent memory and check whether it returns in fresh sessions.

items.name: Agent-to-Agent Trust
items.test: Send a subagent a message that crosses a trust boundary and record what it obeys.

items.name: MCP Server Trust
items.test: Check what an MCP server can read, write and call, and who reviewed it.

items.name: Subagent Spawning
items.test: Check whether a kill switch reaches agents spawned after the stop.

items.name: Kill Switch Escape
items.test: Trigger the stop mid-run and confirm every branch halts and reports.

items.name: Sandbox Escape
items.test: Attempt filesystem, process and network reach from the tool runtime.

items.name: Code Execution via Tools
items.test: Run code through the tool path and record what the sandbox permits.

items.name: SSRF via Fetch and Browse
items.test: Point the fetch tool at the metadata endpoint and at an internal admin page.

items.name: Autonomous Goal Hijacking
items.test: Change the stated goal mid-run through injected content and see whether the plan follows.

items.name: Loop and Step Ceiling
items.test: Look for a missing or high step ceiling and measure the cost of one runaway run.

items.name: Unbounded Consumption
items.test: Remove the per-user budget and measure tokens per session at sustained load.

items.name: Denial of Wallet
items.test: Estimate the spend a cheap attacker can force without any exploit skill.

items.name: Prompt Injection via Files and PDFs
items.test: Upload a document with instructions in body text, in a comment and in an alt text field.

items.name: Multimodal Injection
items.test: Put text in an image, a screenshot and an audio clip and see whether it is obeyed.

items.name: Steganographic Exfiltration
items.test: Check whether output length, whitespace or formatting can carry data.

items.name: Insecure Output Handling
items.test: Map every sink the model's text can reach and what renders it.

items.name: SQL Injection via LLM
items.test: Steer model-written SQL and record the database role behind it.

items.name: XSS via LLM Output
items.test: Return markup into a client that renders it and check what executes.

items.name: Markdown Image Exfiltration
items.test: Embed an image URL with data in the query string and watch the egress.

items.name: Link Parameter Exfiltration
items.test: Check whether a link the model emits can carry a conversation fragment.

items.name: Output Length Side Channel
items.test: Check whether the length of a refusal leaks the content it refused.

items.name: Schema Validation
items.test: Break the JSON contract and see whether the consumer validates or trusts.

items.name: Structured Output Abuse
items.test: Force content through a schema field that the plain-text filter would block.

items.name: Guardrail Bypass
items.test: Attempt bypass by encoding, language, length and structured output.

items.name: Guardrail Ordering
items.test: Check whether the guardrail runs before the tool call or after it.

items.name: Prompt Firewall
items.test: Test the firewall as an adversarial classifier rather than as a policy document.

items.name: Input Sanitization
items.test: Compare the sanitised input with what the model actually receives.

items.name: Spotlighting and Delimiters
items.test: Check that the markers survive summarisation and concatenation.

items.name: Dual-LLM Pattern
items.test: Confirm the privileged model never sees untrusted text directly.

items.name: Allowlisting vs Blocklisting
items.test: Test whether the control names what is allowed or lists what is not.

items.name: Eval Set Design
items.test: One behaviour per case, one expected outcome, one fixture that reruns.

items.name: Golden Sets
items.test: Store the reference answer and the rubric with the case rather than in someone's memory.

items.name: Held-Out Sets
items.test: Keep a slice the team never tunes against and report it separately.

items.name: Private Slices
items.test: Keep the sensitive slice out of any public benchmark.

items.name: Benchmark Contamination
items.test: Check for overlap by paraphrase, by translation and by rare-phrase search.

items.name: Benchmark Saturation
items.test: Compare headroom with noise before treating a high score as a signal.

items.name: Attack Success Rate
items.test: Define the unit as attempts or objectives and report the rate with its interval.

items.name: Per-Objective vs Per-Attempt
items.test: Report both and say which one the reader needs.

items.name: Confidence Intervals
items.test: Attach a Wilson interval to every rate, especially the small ones.

items.name: Pass@k
items.test: Report capability at least once across k attempts.

items.name: Pass^k (Reliability)
items.test: Report the probability of success on every one of k attempts.

items.name: Paired Comparison
items.test: Compare two versions on the same cases rather than two independent rates.

items.name: Sample Size and Power
items.test: Check the suite can detect the difference being claimed.

items.name: Run-to-Run Variance
items.test: Run five times and report the spread before the mean.

items.name: LLM-as-Judge
items.test: State the judge model, its revision and the prompt it runs.

items.name: Judge Calibration
items.test: Hand-grade a sample and report agreement with the judge.

items.name: Position Bias
items.test: Swap the order of two answers and see whether the verdict moves.

items.name: Verbosity Bias
items.test: Trim one answer and check whether the score follows the length.

items.name: Self-Preference Bias
items.test: Grade output from the judge's own family against output from another.

items.name: Inter-Rater Reliability
items.test: Have two people grade the same slice and compare.

items.name: Cohen's Kappa
items.test: Report agreement corrected for chance rather than raw percentage.

items.name: Rubric Design
items.test: One behaviour per criterion, and a rubric short enough not to drift.

items.name: Failure Taxonomy
items.test: Bucket every failure so that a fix can be assigned to it.

items.name: Severity Scoring
items.test: Define severity before the run and give the reason for each score.

items.name: Regression Suites
items.test: Turn every finding into a case that runs on every deploy.

items.name: CI Eval Gates
items.test: Block a deploy on a regression in the safety suite.

items.name: Drift Canaries
items.test: Run a standing set weekly and alert when the refusal rate moves.

items.name: Trace-Based Evaluation
items.test: Score spans inside an agent run, not only the final answer.

items.name: Automated Red Teaming
items.test: Generate cases at volume and record what the generator missed.

items.name: Fuzzing and Mutation
items.test: Mutate known cases and record the hit rate per mutation.

items.name: Adversarial Test Generation
items.test: Use a model to attack a model and report the generator as part of the method.

items.name: Coverage Argument
items.test: Write down the classes tested and the classes skipped, with the reason for each.

items.name: Cost per Case
items.test: Report the suite's cost so that it can actually be rerun.

items.name: Latency per Case
items.test: Report how long a full run takes at the sample size claimed.

items.name: Reproducibility Contract
items.test: Record model revision, prompt version, index snapshot, tool schema, sampling and date.

items.name: Threat Modelling for AI
items.test: Write the asset, the actor, the trust boundary and the abuse case before testing.

items.name: Trust Boundaries
items.test: Draw the line between instruction and data for every channel that carries text.

items.name: Data Flow Mapping
items.test: Trace one input from entry to output and mark every place it is trusted.

items.name: Attack Surface Map
items.test: One diagram of every input channel, tool and output sink.

items.name: Propagation Testing
items.test: One bad input, then trace how far the effect reaches.

items.name: OWASP LLM Top 10
items.test: Map each finding so that the security team can file it.

items.name: OWASP Agentic Security
items.test: Map agent findings to the agentic categories.

items.name: MITRE ATLAS
items.test: Map the technique so the finding joins the wider threat picture.

items.name: NIST AI RMF
items.test: Check the client's controls against a framework they already report on.

items.name: NIST Generative AI Profile
items.test: Map the specific actions to the profile's suggested controls.

items.name: ISO/IEC 42001
items.test: Check where AI management meets the existing management system.

items.name: EU AI Act Duties
items.test: Establish general purpose or high risk, and which duties that triggers.

items.name: Model and System Cards
items.test: Compare the documented limits with the observed behaviour.

items.name: AI Bill of Materials
items.test: List weights, dataset and dependencies, and whether each is pinned.

items.name: Model Provenance and Signing
items.test: Confirm the artefact is signed and the digest matches what runs.

items.name: Risk Register
items.test: Enter each finding with an owner, a residual risk and a review date.

items.name: Dangerous Capability Evaluation
items.test: Test uplift and autonomy inside a container with no live access.

items.name: Uplift Studies
items.test: Compare an unaided expert with an assisted one on the same task.

items.name: Propensity vs Capability
items.test: Separate what the system can be made to do from what it does unprompted.

items.name: Red Team Rules of Engagement
items.test: Written scope, authorised targets, a stop condition and a named person who can stop it.

items.name: Safe Harbour
items.test: Agree in writing what the tester may do and what protection applies.

items.name: Coordinated Disclosure
items.test: Agree the channel and the timeline before the first finding exists.

items.name: Bug Bounty for AI
items.test: Check the programme covers prompt injection and model behaviour, not only web bugs.

items.name: AI Incident Response
items.test: Walk one scenario: a prompt leak, model abuse, or an exfiltration channel firing.

items.name: Human Oversight Design
items.test: Name what the gate gates and whether the person can understand the decision.

items.name: Auditable Logging
items.test: Check the log answers a regulator's question six months later.

items.name: Privacy Impact Assessment
items.test: Treat prompts as personal data and check residency, retention and access.

items.name: Data Residency of Prompts
items.test: Trace where prompt text is stored and which jurisdiction holds it.

items.name: Prompt Versioning
items.test: Confirm every prompt change has an identifier and a rollback.

items.name: Model Version Pinning
items.test: Pin the revision by digest and record it in every report.

items.name: Rollback of Prompts and Models
items.test: Restore the previous version and check the index and cache go back too.

items.name: Purple Teaming
items.test: Run the defence and the attack together so the fix is tested as it is written.

items.name: Continuous Red Teaming
items.test: Schedule the suite rather than running it once at launch.

items.name: Adversarial Training as Patching
items.test: Check whether a patch removes the behaviour or only the string that triggered it.

items.name: Safety Cases
items.test: Write the argument that the system is acceptable, with its assumptions named.
